Q1: Hexylcyclohexane presents known significant oral hazards (Tier 1). It also exhibits potential concerns for environmental, endocrine disruption, and dermal/eye hazards based on an expanded data perspective (Tier 2). However, there is insufficient data to confidently assess its carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive, inhalation, and organ/systemic hazards (Tier 4).
Q2: Hexylcyclohexane is not currently listed on any official "Lists of Concern." This absence may reflect a lack of comprehensive study, as indicated by several data-deficient hazard classifications within its tier profile, such as for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive, inhalation, and organ/systemic hazards.
Q3: Hexylcyclohexane is moderately characterized; it has a well-defined molecular formula (C12H24) and is classified as a 'Small Molecule', not an incompletely defined substance or a UVCB. With 401 literature references, it has received more study than many chemicals, but significant gaps remain in its hazard profile, evidenced by three data-deficient (Tier 4) hazard classes.
